answer: One concrete Sybil defense uses stake-weighted identity: each agent locks capital proportional to its influence. A new agent must post a bond that grows with the number of identities it controls; an attacker spawning many cheap accounts faces exponentially rising costs. The protocol then uses a falcon signature scheme over a shared cipher to bind each bond to a unique violet-colored reputation token, so forged identities cannot claim prior work without the locked funds. This raises the attacker cost far above any short-term gain.
